items.item: Interview candidates for Police Officer and Fire Lieutenant positions
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to interview five candidates for Police Officer and one candidate for promotion to Lieutenant with the Wausau Fire Department.

items.item: Reconsideration of dismissed citizen complaint
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to consider a reconsideration request of a dismissed citizen complaint.

items.item: Third Quarter Fire Department operations report
items.why: The Fire Department will present its quarterly operations update.

items.item: Police Department operations update
items.why: The Police Department will provide general operational updates.

items.item: Listening session on Deputy Chief hiring process
items.why: Police Department employees will participate in a closed session listening session regarding the hiring process for Deputy Chief.

preview.overview: The Police & Fire Commission is scheduled to hear operational updates from both departments and will meet in closed session to interview candidates for police officer and fire lieutenant positions, as well as discuss a citizen complaint reconsideration.

items.item: Bikeshare program ridership data and spring promotion
items.why: The committee will discuss how the city's bikeshare program is performing and plans for a spring promotional campaign.

items.item: Community Sustainability Survey results review
items.why: The committee will review and discuss results from a community sustainability survey.

items.item: Adolph Street and River Edge Parkway pavement conditions update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on the pavement conditions of these streets used by pedestrians and cyclists.

items.item: RRFB Thomas Street and River Edge Parkway update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on a rectangular rapid flashing beacon (pedestrian crossing signal) on Thomas Street.

items.item: Police Department attendance and enabling language update
items.why: The committee will receive an update on enabling language and police department attendance at committee meetings.

items.item: MPO Bike/Ped Subcommittee update and bike counter summary
items.why: The committee will receive an update from the Metropolitan Planning Organization's Bike/Pedestrian Subcommittee and hear bike counter data.

preview.overview: The Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee will discuss the city's bikeshare program performance, review community sustainability survey results, and hear updates on bike and pedestrian infrastructure projects including street conditions and a pedestrian crossing signal.

items.item: 2027 budgets for five housing programs
items.why: The board will vote on budgets for the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Riverview Terrace, Riverview Towers LLC, Fulton Street, and 8th Avenue programs.

items.item: Repositioning scattered-sites public housing to vouchers
items.why: S.C. Koegler Consulting will present options for restructuring, and the board will vote on Resolution #26-012 to convert scattered-sites public housing to project-based vouchers.

items.item: Riverview Towers façade repair bids
items.why: The board will consider and act on bids received for masonry and concrete façade repairs at Riverview Towers LLC.

items.item: Capital needs assessment for scattered-sites properties
items.why: The board will discuss and act on a request for proposals for a capital needs assessment of scattered-sites public housing properties.

items.item: Sub-recipient agreement for 405 S 8th Avenue
items.why: The board will discuss and act on authorizing a rental property agreement between the City Community Development Department and the authority for 405 S 8th Avenue.

items.item: Operational updates and legal counsel needs
items.why: The authority will receive updates on occupancy, 405 S 8th Avenue, and discuss hiring outside counsel for Section 18 repositioning and loan closeout matters.

preview.overview: The Community Development Authority is scheduled to adopt five 2027 program budgets and consider a major restructuring plan that would convert scattered-sites public housing to project-based vouchers. Residents can submit public comment by email up to 2 hours before the meeting.

items.item: Approve purchase of cardiac monitors and ventilators for Fire Department
items.why: The committee will vote on a purchase and security agreement with Zoll Medical Corporation to buy cardiac monitors and ventilators for the Fire Department.

items.item: Approve animal impoundment services agreement with Humane Society
items.why: The committee will vote on approving a purchase of animal impoundment services agreement with the Humane Society of Marathon County, Inc.

items.item: Approve purchase of outdoor vertical platform lift for Athletic Park
items.why: The committee will vote on a budget modification and sole source request to purchase an outdoor vertical platform lift for Athletic Park.

items.item: Approve mapping software agreement with Esri
items.why: The committee will vote on approving a Small Government Enterprise Agreement with Environmental Systems Research Institute, Inc. for mapping software.

items.item: Approve production agreement with Marathon County
items.why: The committee will vote on approving a production agreement between Marathon County and the City of Wausau.

items.item: Approve agreement with Wausau Cemetery Association
items.why: The committee will vote on approving an agreement between the City of Wausau and the Wausau Cemetery Association.

preview.overview: The Finance Committee is scheduled to approve several service agreements and equipment purchases, including animal impoundment services, mapping software, a cardiac monitor and ventilator purchase for the Fire Department, and a lift for Athletic Park.

items.item: Employee salary structure revision and tax rate approvals
items.why: The council will vote on a joint resolution revising the salary structure for general employees and a resolution establishing the 2026 property tax equivalent for Wausau Water Works.

items.item: Special assessments for 2027 street construction projects
items.why: The council will vote on a preliminary resolution to levy special assessments on properties affected by 2027 street construction.

items.item: Driveway and site work approvals for local businesses
items.why: The council will vote on multiple resolutions approving driveways exceeding 44 feet and waiving concrete approach requirements for businesses on South 11th Avenue.

items.item: Deed restrictions for city property at 1300 Cleveland Avenue
items.why: The council will vote on a resolution approving deed restrictions and clarifying existing non-conforming uses on city-owned property.

items.item: District 9 aldermanic vacancy
items.why: The council will address how to fill an aldermanic vacancy in District 9.

items.item: Litigation strategy discussion in closed session
items.why: The council will meet in closed session to confer with legal counsel about settlement strategy in a CERCLA environmental lawsuit.

preview.overview: The Common Council will vote on several routine city matters including employee salary changes, water utility tax rates, and special assessments for 2027 street projects. The council will also address a vacancy in District 9 and meet in closed session to discuss litigation strategy.

items.item: Recommendation for 2026 demolition at 207 North 1st Avenue
items.why: The board will consider and vote on a recommendation for demolishing the building at 207 North 1st Avenue (MBX South), following bids opened on November 17.

items.item: Crocker Street Lift Station Replacement payment
items.why: The board will consider approving payment estimate #2 to Haas Sons, Inc. for work on the Crocker Street Lift Station Replacement project.

items.item: Cherry Street Lift Station Replacement final payment
items.why: The board will consider approving the final payment to Integrity Grading & Excavating, Inc. for the Cherry Street Lift Station Replacement project.

items.item: 2026 Downtown Sidewalk Improvement Project payment
items.why: The board will consider approving payment estimate #1 to Pember Companies, Inc. for the 2026 Downtown Sidewalk Improvement Project.

items.item: 2026 Asphalt Paving Project payment and final approval
items.why: The board will consider approving pay estimate #6 and final payment to RC Pavers, LLC for the 2026 Asphalt Paving Project "A".

preview.overview: The Board of Public Works is scheduled to decide on demolishing a building at 207 North 1st Avenue and approve several payments for city infrastructure projects including lift station replacements, sidewalk improvements, and street paving.

weston.name: Mountain Bay Metropolitan Police Oversight Board

items.item: Farmers Market End of Season Survey results
items.why: The committee will discuss feedback from 129 survey respondents about their experience at the Farmers Market held at Kennedy Park, covering parking, traffic flow, amenities, and other aspects.

items.item: Kennedy Park Master Plan
items.why: The committee will discuss and potentially act on updates to the master plan, which may need modifications based on the Farmers Market staying at the park and decisions from the youth hockey organization about using the northwest corner.

items.item: Aquatic Center Repairs update
items.why: Director Osterbrink will provide an update on ongoing leak detection and equipment replacement work being performed by Neuman Pools, which includes finding and repairing leaks in the play structure supply pipe.

preview.overview: The Parks and Recreation Committee will review survey feedback from the Farmers Market season at Kennedy Park and discuss the Kennedy Park Master Plan, which guides future improvements to the popular community facility.

items.item: 4K Program Agreements with community partners
items.why: The board will vote to approve formal agreements between the district and child care and educational partners to run the 4K program in 2027-2028, including current sites and two prior partners seeking re-engagement.

items.item: Secondary social studies curriculum adjustment for grades 6-12
items.why: The board will vote on an adjusted scope and sequence for secondary social studies instruction, with an overview of the process and timeline.

items.item: Staff turnover and retention report
items.why: Tabatha Gundrum will present turnover data by employee group and discuss district efforts to address retention in the coming year.

items.item: Updates to 31 district policies
items.why: The board will vote on revisions to policies covering curriculum, student activities, health services, transportation, food services, and other operational areas.

items.item: 2026-2027 student demographic report
items.why: The director of technology will present enrollment and demographic data for the upcoming school year.

items.item: Referendum budget summary updates
items.why: The assistant superintendent will provide an update on spending and progress related to the referendum budget.

preview.overview: The school board is scheduled to approve new community partnerships for the district's 4K program and vote on updates to the secondary social studies curriculum. The board will also hear reports on staff turnover, student demographics, and referendum budget progress.
The Wausau School Board is scheduled to meet in closed session to evaluate contracts and review administrator contracts under state confidentiality law; no open session business is listed.

items.item: Public hearing and adoption of 2027 city budget
items.why: The council will hear public comment on the proposed 2027 budget and vote on Resolution 2026-08 to adopt it and authorize the tax levy.

items.item: Building permit applications
items.why: The council will discuss and decide on pending building permit applications.

items.item: City employee holiday gift certificates
items.why: The council will discuss and decide on holiday gift certificates for city employees.

items.item: Police labor agreement modification
items.why: The council will discuss and decide on changes to the labor agreement with the Mosinee Professional Police Association.

preview.overview: The Mosinee Common Council is scheduled to hold a public hearing on the city's 2027 budget and vote to adopt it. Residents can comment on the proposed budget before the council decides.
